Class PoolEvictor

java.lang.Object
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.core.pool.PoolEvictor
public final class PoolEvictor extends Object
Shrinks idle Vibur object pools so that objects which are expensive to retain — XML parsers and JAX-WS client stubs in particular — do not stay allocated after a traffic burst has passed.

This is the equivalent of Commons Pool's timeBetweenEvictionRunsMillis plus minEvictableIdleTime, and it follows the same algorithm as Vibur's own SamplingPoolReducer: within each eviction interval the pool is sampled SAMPLES_PROPERTY times, the smallest observed number of idle objects is remembered, and at the end of the interval that many objects are destroyed. Sampling the minimum rather than the instantaneous count is what makes this safe — only objects that stayed idle for the whole interval are considered evictable.

Unlike SamplingPoolReducer, which allocates one daemon thread per pool, this evictor drives every registered pool from a single shared daemon thread. That matters because IPF creates one client-stub pool per web-service endpoint, and those pools come and go with Camel routes. Pools are held through a WeakReference, so a pool belonging to a discarded endpoint is dropped automatically at the next run and neither the pool nor its objects are leaked.

Eviction is capped at MAX_REDUCTION_FRACTION of the created objects per interval so that a pool shrinks gradually instead of collapsing, and it never reduces a pool below its configured initial size.

Setting EVICTION_INTERVAL_PROPERTY to 0 or a negative value disables eviction altogether; no thread is then created.

Since:
6.0

  • Field Details

    • EVICTION_INTERVAL_PROPERTY

      public static final String EVICTION_INTERVAL_PROPERTY
      System property controlling the length of one eviction interval, in milliseconds. Defaults to 60000L. Zero or negative disables eviction.

    • SAMPLES_PROPERTY

      public static final String SAMPLES_PROPERTY
      System property controlling how often a pool is sampled within one eviction interval. Defaults to 6.

  • Method Details

    • register

      public static void register(org.vibur.objectpool.BasePool pool, String name)
      Registers a pool for idle eviction. Registration does not prevent the pool from being garbage collected; callers therefore need no matching deregistration step.
      Parameters:
      pool - the pool to shrink when it holds objects that stay idle, not null
      name - a short name used in log output
